items.title: Undistorted Practice: Learning Correctly, Without Pride or Private Opinion

items.zh: 云何名為無倒加行？謂如善達修瑜伽行諸瑜伽師之所開悟，即如是學，於法、於義不顛倒取，無有我慢，亦不安住自所見取，無邪僻執，於尊教誨終不輕毀。如是名為無倒加行。
items.en: What is undistorted practice? That is, exactly as one is instructed by teachers well versed in yogic practice, one learns accordingly — grasping neither the teaching nor its meaning in a distorted way, without arrogance, not settling into one's own private views, free of deviant clinging, and never disparaging the instruction of one's venerable teachers. This is called undistorted practice.

items.title: Section: Timely Practice Opens — Stillness, Insight, Energizing, and Equanimizing

items.zh: 云何名為應時加行？謂於時時間修習止相，於時時間修習觀相，於時時間修習舉相，於時時間修習捨相。又能如實了知其止、止相、止時；了知其觀、觀相、觀時；了知其舉、舉相、舉時；了知其捨、捨相、捨時。
items.en: What is timely practice? That is, at the fitting time, one cultivates the mark of stillness; at the fitting time, one cultivates the mark of insight; at the fitting time, one cultivates the mark of energizing; and at the fitting time, one cultivates the mark of equanimizing. Further, one correctly and truly knows stillness, its mark, and its proper time; knows insight, its mark, and its proper time; knows energizing, its mark, and its proper time; and knows equanimizing, its mark, and its proper time.

items.zh: 云何為止？謂九相心住。能令其心無相、無分別、寂靜、極寂靜、等住寂止、純一無雜，故名為止。云何止相？謂有二種。一、所緣相，二、因緣相。所緣相者，謂奢摩他品所知事同分影像，是名所緣相。由此所緣，令心寂靜。因緣相者，謂依奢摩他所熏習心，為令後時奢摩他定皆清淨故，修習瑜伽毘鉢舍那所有加行，是名因緣相。云何止時？謂心掉舉時，或恐掉舉時，是修止時。
items.en: What is stillness? It is the nine stages of mental abiding, which cause the mind to become free of marks, free of discursive thought, tranquil, thoroughly tranquil, evenly abiding at rest, and singly unified without admixture — hence it is called stillness. Its object-mark is the image of the same type as the object of knowledge belonging to the calm-abiding type; through this object, the mind becomes tranquil. Its causal mark is that, relying on the mind trained by calm-abiding, in order that calm-abiding's concentration may become ever more purified in the future, one cultivates the entire practice of insight — this is its causal mark. What is the proper time for stillness? When the mind is agitated, or on the verge of becoming agitated, this is the time to cultivate stillness.

items.zh: 又依毘鉢舍那所熏習心，為諸尋思之所擾惱及諸事業所擾惱時，是修止時。

items.title: Section: Insight, Energizing, and Equanimizing — Timely Practice Completes

items.zh: 云何為觀？謂四行、三門、六事差別所緣觀行。云何觀相？謂有二種。一、所緣相。二、因緣相。所緣相者，謂毘鉢舍那品所知事同分影像。由此所緣，令慧觀察。因緣相者，謂依毘鉢舍那所熏習心，為令後時毘鉢舍那皆清淨故，修習內心奢摩他定所有加行。云何觀時？謂心沈沒時，或恐沈沒時，是修觀時。又依奢摩他所熏習心，先應於彼所知事境如實覺了，故於爾時是修觀時。
items.en: What is insight? It is the fourfold wisdom-conduct, the three gates, and the contemplation with objects differentiated by the six things. Its object-mark is the image of the same type as the object of knowledge belonging to the insight type; through this object, wisdom investigates. Its causal mark is that, relying on the mind trained by insight, in order that insight may become ever more purified in the future, one cultivates the entire practice of inward calm-abiding concentration. What is the proper time for insight? When the mind is sinking, or on the verge of sinking, this is the time to cultivate insight. Further, relying on the mind trained by calm-abiding, one should first correctly understand the object of knowledge as it truly is — this too is the time to cultivate insight.

items.zh: 云何為舉？謂由隨取一種淨妙所緣境界，顯示、勸導、慶慰其心。云何舉相？謂由淨妙所緣境界，策勵其心，及彼隨順發勤精進。云何舉時？謂心沈下時，或恐沈下時，是修舉時。云何為捨？謂於所緣心無染污、心平等性，於止觀品調柔正直任運轉性，及調柔心有堪能性，令心隨與任運作用。云何捨相？謂由所緣令心上捨，及於所緣不發所有太過精進。云何捨時？謂於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那品，所有掉舉心已解脫，是修捨時。如是名為應時加行。
items.en: What is energizing? It is taking up whichever pure, excellent object inspires the mind, displaying it, urging oneself on with it, and consoling the mind through it. What is the proper time for energizing? When the mind is sinking low, or on the verge of sinking low, this is the time to cultivate energizing. What is equanimizing? It is a mind, with respect to its object, free of defilement, evenly balanced … letting the mind proceed spontaneously in its function. What is the proper time for equanimizing? When the mind, whether in calm-abiding or insight, has already been freed of all agitation, this is the time to cultivate equanimizing. This is called timely practice.

items.title: Understanding Practice: Freedom to Enter, Abide In, and Rise From Concentration

items.zh: 云何名為解了加行？謂於如是所說諸相善取、善了。善取了已，欲入定時即便能入，欲住定時即便能住，欲起定時即便能起。或時棄捨諸三摩地所行影像，作意思惟諸不定地所有本性所緣境界。如是名為解了加行。
items.en: What is understanding practice? That is, skilfully grasping and skilfully comprehending all the marks just described. Having skilfully grasped and comprehended them, when one wishes to enter concentration, one is able to enter it; when one wishes to abide in concentration, one is able to abide in it; when one wishes to rise from concentration, one is able to rise from it. At times, one sets aside the image belonging to samādhi's own activity and directs attention instead to the original object belonging to the non-concentrated state. This is called understanding practice.

items.title: Section: Insatiable Practice Opens — Never Settling for "Enough"

items.zh: 云何名為無厭足加行？謂於善法無有厭足，修斷無廢，於展轉上、展轉勝處，多住希求。
items.en: What is insatiable practice? That is, never being satisfied with wholesome states, never ceasing to cultivate and to sever, and continually dwelling in the aspiration for ever higher, ever more excellent states.

items.title: Insatiable Practice Continued: Never Retreating Midway

items.zh: 不唯獲得少小靜定，便於中路而生退屈。於餘所作，常有進求。如是名為無厭足加行。
items.en: One does not, merely upon attaining some slight measure of stillness, grow discouraged and retreat midway. Towards whatever else remains to be accomplished, one constantly presses forward in pursuit. This is called insatiable practice.

items.title: Section: Unabandoning Practice — Precepts as the Yoke That Keeps the Mind from Scattering

items.zh: 云何名為不捨軛加行？謂於一切所受學處，無穿、無缺；雖見少年顏容端正可愛母邑，而不取相、不取隨好；於食平等；勤修覺寤；少事、少業、少諸散亂；於久所作、久所說等，能自隨憶，令他隨憶。如是等法，說名不捨軛加行。
items.en: What is unabandoning practice? That is, with respect to every precept one has undertaken, neither breaking nor lacking any of them; though seeing a young woman of attractive, pleasing appearance, not grasping at her general appearance nor at her alluring details; being even-handed regarding food; diligently cultivating wakefulness; having few affairs, little activity, and little distraction; and being able, oneself, to recall — and to help others recall — what was done and said long ago. Such practices as these are called unabandoning practice.

items.zh: 由此諸法，能正隨順心一境性，不捨其軛，令心不散；不令其心馳流外境；不令其心內不調柔。如是名為不捨軛加行。
items.en: Through these various practices, one rightly accords with one-pointedness of mind, never setting down this yoke, keeping the mind from scattering — not letting the mind race outward towards external objects, and not letting the mind remain inwardly unyielding. This is called unabandoning practice.

blocks.text: Five more kinds of good practice. The section on "timely practice" is one of the clearest instructions in the treatise on balancing a meditation session.
"Exactly as one is instructed by teachers well versed in yoga, one learns accordingly, without arrogance, not settling into one's own private views."
At the right time, stillness; at the right time, insight; at the right time, energising; at the right time, equanimity.

items: **Stillness** is the nine stages of mental abiding. Its time: "when the mind is agitated, or on the verge of agitation".

**Insight** is the four kinds of wisdom-conduct, three gates, and six things. Its time: "when the mind is sinking, or on the verge of sinking"; and also, with a mind already trained by calm, when one should first understand the object as it truly is.
**Energising**: "taking up whichever pure, excellent object inspires the mind". Its time: "when the mind is sinking low, or on the verge of sinking".
**Equanimity**: a mind "evenly balanced", letting it "proceed spontaneously". Its time: "when the mind, whether in calm or insight, has already been freed of all agitation".

blocks.text: Skilfully grasping these marks, "when one wishes to enter concentration, one is able to enter it; to abide, abide; to rise, rise". Master Cháng Bǎi: at times one sets aside the image and returns to the original object.
"Never being satisfied with wholesome states", and "not, upon attaining some slight measure of stillness, growing discouraged and retreating midway".
Keeping every precept; guarding the senses; moderate in food; wakeful; few affairs. "Never setting down this yoke, keeping the mind from scattering."

quiz.q: Undistorted practice: "not settling into one's own views." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: don't stay stuck in one's own opinions
quiz.why: "Without arrogance, not settling into one's own private views, free of deviant clinging, and never disparaging the instruction of one's venerable teachers." Venerable Miào Jìng: do not stay fixed in your own views.

quiz.q: Stillness makes the mind "markless and non-discursive." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: non-discursive is of the mind, markless of the object
quiz.why: "Which cause the mind to become free of marks, free of discursive thought, tranquil … hence it is called stillness." Venerable Miào Jìng: "non-discursive" is said of the mind; "markless" of the object.

quiz.q: "When the mind is agitated, it is time for stillness." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say agitation usually is?
options: recalling past pleasures, like gathering for tea and fun
quiz.why: "What is the proper time for stillness? When the mind is agitated, or on the verge of becoming agitated." Master Cháng Bǎi: agitation usually comes from recalling past pleasures — friends gathering, drinking tea, having fun.

quiz.q: "When the mind is sinking, it is time for insight." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe sinking?
options: losing the object without wandering thoughts — easily mistaken for absorption
quiz.why: "What is the proper time for insight? When the mind is sinking, or on the verge of sinking." Venerable Miào Jìng: the object is lost, yet there are no wandering thoughts — easily mistaken for absorption; this is sinking.

quiz.q: Equanimity is "a mind undefiled and even towards its object." How do the masters explain "superior equanimity"?
options: Miào Jìng: discarding everything incompatible; Cháng Bǎi: "superior" means strength to cast off hindrances, free of torpor and agitation
quiz.why: "What is the proper time for equanimizing? When the mind, whether in calm-abiding or insight, has already been freed of all agitation." Venerable Miào Jìng: "superior equanimity" means discarding everything incompatible. Master Cháng Bǎi: "superior" means having strength — strength to cast off hindrances and distraction, so equanimity appears, free of torpor and agitation.

quiz.q: Understanding practice sometimes sets aside samādhi's image for "the original object." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: before was a similar image; now the original itself, not an image
quiz.why: "At times, one sets aside the image belonging to samādhi's own activity and directs attention instead to the original object belonging to the non-concentrated state." Venerable Miào Jìng: before, it was a same-type object — a similar image; now it is the original, not an image.

quiz.q: "修斷無廢" is rendered "never abandoning the cultivation of what is to be severed." How do the lectures read it?
options: both: never stop practising to cut affliction; the English reads as if cultivating what is to be cut
quiz.why: "Never being satisfied with wholesome states, never abandoning the cultivation of what is to be severed." Venerable Miào Jìng: cultivating calm and insight to cut affliction never stops. Master Cháng Bǎi: don't be quickly satisfied with calm and insight; don't abandon the practice of cutting affliction — keep advancing. The English reads as if one cultivates what is to be cut.
